Title: Verify that an application allowed `offline_access` receives a refresh token when the authorization request asks for that scope
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- `EnableOAuth2V1` is on.
- App A's consent policy allows `offline_access`.
- Tester has a customer account that can sign in to GK One.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- App A holds a refresh token (RT1) for the customer.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Smoke

Step Action:
Set App A's authorization request scope to include `openid profile email offline_access`.
Postman: collection variables → confirm `scope` = `openid profile email offline_access`.

Sign in as the customer and exchange the authorization code for tokens.
Postman: 02 · Build the sign-in URL → open the console URL in a browser and sign in → paste `code` into `authCode` → 02 · Exchange code for tokens.
Step Expected: Sign-in completes and the token response is returned.

Step Action:
Inspect the raw token response.
Postman: 02 · Exchange code for tokens → response body and console.
Step Expected: Response contains an `access_token`, an `id_token` and a `refresh_token`.

Title: Verify that an application allowed `offline_access` receives no refresh token and no error when the authorization request does not ask for that scope
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A's consent policy allows `offline_access`.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- App A holds no refresh token from this sign-in.
- Postman `scope` variable is set back to `openid profile email offline_access`.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API

Step Action:
Set App A's authorization request scope to `openid profile email` (no `offline_access`).
Postman: collection variables → set `scope` = `openid profile email`.

Sign in as the customer and exchange the authorization code for tokens.
Postman: 02 · Build the sign-in URL → browser sign-in → paste `code` into `authCode` → 02 · Exchange code for tokens.
Step Expected: Sign-in completes without an error.

Step Action:
Inspect the raw token response.
Postman: 02 · Exchange code for tokens → response body and console.
Step Expected: Response contains an `access_token` and an `id_token`. No `refresh_token` is present.

Title: Verify that an application not allowed `offline_access` is refused with `invalid_scope` when the authorization request asks for that scope
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App B's consent policy does not allow `offline_access`.
- App B has `https://oauth.pstmn.io/v1/callback` registered as a redirect URI.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- No tokens are issued to App B.
- Postman `clientId` and `clientSecret` are set back to App A's values.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Negative

Step Action:
Build an authorization request for App B with scope `openid profile email offline_access` and valid PKCE parameters.
Postman: set `clientId` and `clientSecret` to App B's values, keep `scope` with `offline_access` → 02 · Build the sign-in URL.

Send the request to `/authorize`.
Postman: open the console URL in a browser.
Step Expected: Request is refused with `invalid_scope` (shown as `error=invalid_scope` in the address bar). No sign-in screen is reached and no authorization code is issued.

Title: Verify that an application can exchange a refresh token for new tokens without the customer signing in again
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds AT1, IT1 and RT1 from a sign-in that asked for `offline_access` (Postman: SIGN IN, then copy `accessToken`, `idToken`, `refreshToken` into `at1`, `it1`, `rt1`).
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- App A holds a working AT2 and RT2.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Smoke

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Response is `200` and contains a new `access_token` (AT2), a new `id_token` (IT2) and a new `refresh_token` (RT2). No sign-in screen or customer interaction is required.

Step Action:
Compare AT2, IT2 and RT2 with AT1, IT1 and RT1.
Postman: compare the refresh response body with `at1`, `it1`, `rt1`.
Step Expected: All three are different values from the originals.

Step Action:
Call `/userinfo` with AT2.
Postman: 01 · Userinfo, and capture the token.
Step Expected: Response is `200` and returns the same customer.

Title: Verify that the ID token returned by a refresh keeps the original `auth_time`, carries no `nonce`, and the refreshed tokens keep the original scopes
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds IT1 and RT1 from a sign-in that asked for `openid profile email offline_access` (Postman: SIGN IN).
- IT1 has been decoded and its `auth_time` and scopes noted (Postman: decode `idToken` at jwt.io).
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- Refreshing has not been treated as a new sign-in.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; OpenID Connect; Token Refresh; API

Step Action: Wait at least one minute after sign-in, so a changed `auth_time` would be visible.

Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: New tokens (AT2, IT2, RT2) are returned.

Step Action:
Decode IT2 and compare its `auth_time` with IT1's.
Postman: copy `id_token` from the refresh response body (it is not saved to a variable) → decode at jwt.io.
Step Expected: `auth_time` in IT2 is identical to IT1's.

Step Action:
Check IT2 for a `nonce` claim.
Postman: same decoded `id_token`.
Step Expected: IT2 carries no `nonce`.

Step Action:
Check the `scope` value in the refresh response, or introspect AT2.
Postman: refresh response body, or 01 · Introspect the access token.
Step Expected: Scopes are the same as the original grant (`openid profile email offline_access`) — no scope added or dropped.

Title: Verify that a refreshed access token reports active at introspection and the replaced access token keeps its own expiry
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds AT1 and RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN, then copy `accessToken` into `at1`).
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- AT2 is active for 1 hour from issue.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: AT2 and RT2 are returned.

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT2.
Postman: 01 · Introspect the access token (bearer and body both `{{accessToken}}`).
Step Expected: `active: true`, with an expiry 1 hour after AT2 was issued.

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT1.
Postman: 01 · Introspect the access token with body `token` = `{{at1}}`.
Step Expected: Record the result. AT1 is still within its 1-hour lifetime; refreshing is not documented as deactivating it.

Title: Verify that a refreshed access token reports inactive at introspection once its 1-hour lifetime has passed
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds AT2 from a refresh, with its issue time noted (Postman: SIGN IN → 02 · Refresh the access token → copy `accessToken` into `tc7` → decode at jwt.io and note `exp`).
- The customer does not sign in to App A again until the test completes — a new sign-in was observed to deactivate earlier access tokens.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- An expired refreshed access token is treated the same as any expired access token.
- Postman bearer on 01 · Userinfo is set back to `{{accessToken}}`.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Regression

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT2 shortly before 1 hour after issue.
Postman: 01 · Introspect the access token with body `token` = `{{tc7}}`.
Step Expected: `active: true`.

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT2 just after 1 hour after issue.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token (for a fresh bearer) → 01 · Introspect the access token with body `token` = `{{tc7}}`.
Step Expected: `active: false`.

Step Action:
Call `/userinfo` with AT2.
Postman: 01 · Userinfo, and capture the token with the bearer temporarily set to `{{tc7}}`.
Step Expected: Response is `401`.

Title: Verify that a refresh token cannot be used again after it has been exchanged
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN, then copy `refreshToken` into `rt1`).
- Postman has a "Refresh with old token" request: a copy of 02 · Refresh the access token whose body `refresh_token` is set to the old token variable.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- RT1 is permanently unusable.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Security; Negative

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: New tokens including RT2 are returned.

Step Action:
Send a second refresh request with RT1.
Postman: Refresh with old token (body `refresh_token` = `{{rt1}}`).
Step Expected: Request is rejected (expected `invalid_grant`). No tokens are returned.

Title: Verify that the current refresh token keeps working after an old, replaced refresh token is presented
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN, then copy `refreshToken` into `rt1`).
- Postman has the "Refresh with old token" request.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- Only the reused old token was rejected; App A's access continues on RT3.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Edge Case

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: RT2 is returned.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1 again.
Postman: Refresh with old token (body `refresh_token` = `{{rt1}}`).
Step Expected: Request is rejected.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT2.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Response is `200` and returns AT3, IT3 and RT3. The grant has not been revoked by the reuse attempt.

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT3.
Postman: 01 · Introspect the access token.
Step Expected: `active: true`.

Title: Verify that repeated refreshes each replace the previous refresh token
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN).
- Postman has the "Refresh with old token" request.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- Only the most recently issued refresh token works at any point in the chain.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Regression

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token, then copy `refreshToken` into `rt2`.
Step Expected: RT2 is returned.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT2.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: RT3 is returned.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT3.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: RT4 is returned.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT2.
Postman: Refresh with old token (body `refresh_token` = `{{rt2}}`).
Step Expected: Request is rejected.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT4.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Response is `200` and returns RT5.

Title: Verify that a refresh token keeps working after the customer signs out, while their access tokens are deactivated
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- Customer has signed in to App A with `offline_access`; App A holds AT1 and RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN, then copy `accessToken` into `at1`).
- The `end_session_endpoint` URL has been taken from the discovery document (Postman: 04 · End session prints it).
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- The GK One session is ended, but App A's offline access survives through the refresh token.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; Session; API; Edge Case

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT1.
Postman: 01 · Introspect the access token.
Step Expected: `active: true`.

Step Action:
In the same browser session used to sign in, go to the `end_session_endpoint` (`/logout`).
Postman: open `https://app-gkone-identity-001-dev.azurewebsites.net/logout` in the browser used for SIGN IN.
Step Expected: Customer is signed out of GK One and the GK One session cookie is cleared.

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT1.
Postman: 01 · Introspect the access token.
Step Expected: `active: false` (a `401` on the call also means AT1 is dead, as AT1 is the bearer).

Step Action:
Call `/userinfo` with AT1.
Postman: 01 · Userinfo, and capture the token.
Step Expected: Response is `401`.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Response is `200` and returns AT2, IT2 and RT2.

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT2.
Postman: 01 · Introspect the access token.
Step Expected: `active: true`.

Title: Verify that refreshing tokens does not keep the customer's GK One session alive for other applications after sign-out
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- Customer has signed in to App A with `offline_access` in a browser; App A holds RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN).
- App B is registered with `https://oauth.pstmn.io/v1/callback` as a redirect URI.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- App A still has access through its refresh token.
- No GK One session exists in the browser until the customer signs in again.
- Postman `clientId`, `clientSecret` and `scope` are set back to App A's values.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; SSO; Session; Edge Case

Step Action:
In the same browser, go to the `end_session_endpoint` (`/logout`).
Postman: open `https://app-gkone-identity-001-dev.azurewebsites.net/logout` in the browser used for SIGN IN.
Step Expected: Customer is signed out of GK One.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: New tokens are returned.

Step Action:
In the same browser, start an authorization request for App B.
Postman: set `clientId` and `clientSecret` to App B's values and `scope` = `openid profile email` → 02 · Build the sign-in URL → open the console URL in the same browser.
Step Expected: The ordinary GK One sign-in screen is shown. The customer is not silently signed in to App B.

Title: Verify that a refresh token stops working when the customer removes the application from their account portal
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- Customer has signed in to App A with `offline_access`; App A holds AT1 and RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN).
- App A appears in the customer's linked applications at `/account`.
- Run this case once with a first-party application and once with a third-party application, if both are registered (Postman: swap `clientId` and `clientSecret` to that application's values).
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- App A has no working tokens for the customer.
- The customer's GK One session is unaffected.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; Account Management; Web; Regression

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token, then copy `accessToken` into `at2`.
Step Expected: RT2 is returned.

Step Action:
Signed in as the customer, go to `/account` and revoke App A, confirming the prompt.
Postman: open `https://app-gkone-identity-001-dev.azurewebsites.net/account` in the browser used for SIGN IN.
Step Expected: App A disappears from the linked applications list without a page reload.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT2.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Request is rejected (expected `invalid_grant`). No tokens are returned.

Step Action:
Call `/introspect` with AT2.
Postman: 01 · Introspect the access token with body `token` = `{{at2}}`.
Step Expected: `active: false` (a `401` on the call also means AT2 is dead).

Title: Verify that a refresh token stops working when the application revokes it through `/revoke`
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN).
- Postman has a "Revoke token" request: a copy of 02 · Refresh the access token with URL `{{issuer}}/revoke`, body `token={{refreshToken}}`, `client_id={{clientId}}`, `client_secret={{clientSecret}}`, and no test script.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- RT1 is permanently unusable.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Regression

Step Action:
Send `POST /oauth2/v1/revoke` with `token=` and App A's `client_id` and `client_secret`.
Postman: Revoke token.
Step Expected: Response is `200`.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Request is rejected (expected `invalid_grant`). No tokens are returned.

Title: Verify that a new sign-in to the same application replaces the previous refresh token
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- Customer has signed in to App A with `offline_access`; App A holds RT1 (Postman: SIGN IN, then copy `refreshToken` into `rt1`).
- Postman has the "Refresh with old token" request.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- Only the refresh token from the latest sign-in works.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Edge Case

Step Action:
In the same browser/Postman session, sign in to App A again with `offline_access` (use `prompt=login` if a session is still live).
Postman: 02 · Build the sign-in URL → add `&prompt=login` to the console URL → open it in the same browser and sign in → paste `code` into `authCode` → 02 · Exchange code for tokens.
Step Expected: A new refresh token (RT1-new) is returned.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1 (the original).
Postman: Refresh with old token (body `refresh_token` = `{{rt1}}`).
Step Expected: Request is rejected.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1-new.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Response is `200` and returns new tokens.

Title: Verify that a refresh request is rejected with `invalid_client` when the client secret is wrong or missing
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds a current, unused refresh token (RT1) (Postman: SIGN IN).
- Postman has a "Refresh, bad secret" request: a copy of 02 · Refresh the access token.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- The failed attempts did not use up or revoke RT1.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Security; Negative

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1 and App A's `client_id`, but an incorrect `client_secret`.
Postman: Refresh, bad secret with body `client_secret` = `wrong`.
Step Expected: Request is rejected with `invalid_client` (expected status `401`). No tokens are returned.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1 and App A's `client_id`, with no `client_secret`.
Postman: Refresh, bad secret with the `client_secret` row unticked.
Step Expected: Request is rejected with `invalid_client`. No tokens are returned.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1 and App A's correct `client_id` and `client_secret`.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Response is `200` and returns new tokens.

Title: Verify that a refresh token issued to one application cannot be redeemed with another application's credentials
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A holds a current refresh token (RT1) (Postman: SIGN IN).
- App B's `client_id` and `client_secret` are known.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- App B has received no tokens for the customer.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Security; Negative

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1 using App B's `client_id` and `client_secret`.
Postman: Refresh, bad secret with body `client_id` and `client_secret` typed in as App B's values (variables unchanged) and `refresh_token` = `{{refreshToken}}`.
Step Expected: Request is rejected with `invalid_grant` (expected status `400`). No tokens are returned.

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1 using App A's credentials.
Postman: 02 · Refresh the access token.
Step Expected: Record whether RT1 still works after the cross-client attempt.

Title: Verify that a refresh request with an invalid or missing refresh token is rejected
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A's `client_id` and `client_secret` are known.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- No tokens are issued.
Tags: GK ID; OAuth; Token Refresh; API; Negative

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with `refresh_token` set to a made-up value.
Postman: Refresh with old token with body `refresh_token` = `made-up-value`.
Step Expected: Request is rejected (expected `invalid_grant`).

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with RT1 with one character changed.
Postman: Refresh with old token with body `refresh_token` = a real refresh token with one character changed.
Step Expected: Request is rejected (expected `invalid_grant`).

Step Action:
Send a refresh request with the `refresh_token` parameter left out.
Postman: Refresh with old token with the `refresh_token` row unticked.
Step Expected: Request is rejected (expected `invalid_request`).

Title: Verify that a token request with a grant type other than `authorization_code` or `refresh_token` returns `unsupported_grant_type`
Preconditions:
Pre Conditions:
The following should be true before proceeding:
- App A's `client_id` and `client_secret` are known.
Postconditions:
Post Conditions:
The following should be true after test completion:
- No tokens are issued.
- Postman 03 · Token with an unsupported grant type body is set back to `client_credentials`.

Step Action:
Send `POST /token` with `grant_type=client_credentials`.
Postman: 03 · Token with an unsupported grant type.
Step Expected: Response is `unsupported_grant_type`.

Step Action:
Send `POST /token` with `grant_type=password`.
Postman: 03 · Token with an unsupported grant type with body `grant_type` = `password`.
Step Expected: Response is `unsupported_grant_type`.

Step Action:
Send `POST /token` with `grant_type=made_up_value`.
Postman: 03 · Token with an unsupported grant type with body `grant_type` = `made_up_value`.
Step Expected: Response is `unsupported_grant_type`.
